brief.text:
Every hiker believes these three things about insoles, all three are wrong.

Lie number one, gel insoles stop the pain.

No they don't, you're just padding the problem.

That gel flattens by mile 9 and the pressure still slams your heel every step.

You’re not relieving anything, you’re just hiding it. 
	
Lie number two, sore feet are just part of hiking.
	
That’s what I believed for 10 years.

Then my buddy on a backpacking trip let me try his spare pair of Stepprs.

They’re built with firm massage nodes, and the nodes actually redistribute the load.

So instead of just slightly cushioning your heel and arch like gel insoles, with Stepprs the pressure spreads off the spots that hurt.

15 miles into the day, my feet felt like mile one still.  

To be honest, I thought something was wrong.
